title: fix(spec): a truncated-history build judges a commit by the anchor it records, never by origin/main
body:
Fixes #24359
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`packages/spec/scripts/build-schemas.ts` computes ONE baseline for its three git-reading ratchets: the schema removal check, the authorable-key deletion check and the default-change check. Where `merge-base HEAD origin/main` answers, nothing changes: that is the path this repository's own PR and merge-queue gate runs (`Type Check · source gates` checks out with `fetch-depth: 0`).

Where history is truncated, which is every `--depth=1` rebuild of a pinned commit, the old resolver picked its anchor in this order:

1. the tree's own `authorable-surface.base.json` `baseRev`, but only if origin/main vouched for it;
2. otherwise the rev **origin/main's** anchor names;
3. otherwise **origin/main's tip**.

Arms 2 and 3 make the verdict about commit X a function of where main points when the build runs.

Now a truncated history always anchors on the rev **the tree under test records**. Its keys, manifest and defaults are still read out of git at that rev (never out of the file), and the file is still checked against them. With no anchor the tree can read, the run refuses: either the file is missing, or its `baseRev` cannot be fetched. It never falls back to the tip. `--update-base` is the one mode that still reads the tip in a truncated history, unchanged; moving an existing anchor still refuses there (the forward-only rule).

Per ratchet in the file (measured, not assumed):
- the manifest removal check, the authorable-key deletion check and the default-change check all read the single `resolveSurfaceBase()` resolution, so all three share the defect and all three get this change at once;
- the never-published ratchet (`lib/unemitted-schemas`) and the dropped-refinement ratchet read only in-tree baselines (no git reads), so neither shares the defect and neither changes.

## Measured: the release commit, rebuilt the way objectui rebuilds it

The commit `@objectstack/spec@18.0.0-next.3` was released from, `2c9bf9430a`, rebuilt with `pnpm gen:schema` in an objectui-shaped clone: `git init`, a remote, a depth-1 fetch of the pin. Its `build-schemas.ts` is byte-identical to main's, so "after" means that commit with this script copied in. Every leg's anchor rev is `85c6d76ec42a` unless stated otherwise.

| remote the clone fetches `main` from | before (script `a266dcd7e296`) | after (script `48aab23a9e72`) |
|---|---|---|
| real GitHub main (`71fa166e96` before, `e22defb13c` after) | exit 0, anchored on `85c6d76ec42a` (main still names the same anchor) | exit 0, anchored on `85c6d76ec42a` |
| a main whose anchor commit cannot be fetched (models the objectui CI jobs; see notes) | **exit 1**: anchors on the TIP; `3 schema(s) left the published set with no registered removal`: `api/PackageInstallManifest`, `security/DefaultRowScope`, `ui/PageRecordBinding`, all added on main after the release | exit 1, an accurate refusal: the anchor commit was not served, so the run refuses rather than judge the tree against main or skip the checks |
| a main that re-anchored past the release (synthetic commit `07857fe78f` on the tip, as `--update-base` writes it) | **exit 1**: anchors on main's anchor rev `71fa166e965a`; the same 3 schemas | exit 0, anchored on `85c6d76ec42a` |
| no remote (objectui's workaround) | exit 0, offline in-tree anchor | exit 0, offline in-tree anchor |

So for every origin/main (the real tip, a re-anchored main, none) the release commit gets the same verdict on the same anchor. The only red after the change is a remote that will not serve the commit's own anchor, and that red says exactly that.

objectui's real failure (PR objectui#12963, the `Type Check` job's annotation) matches the before/fetch-failure leg message for message. First "no upstream anchor was usable either … anchors on the origin/main TIP `51ad8e4fba87`", then `❌ 2 schema(s) left the published set …`. At that tip main's own anchor also named `85c6d76ec42a`, so the old resolver's arm 1 was lost only because the anchor fetch failed in that job.

## Ruling ③: the ratchet does not weaken where it guards

The ratchet's own refusal pins (the `a deleted manifest key must prove itself` block): the bypass repro is **red** on a removal, a declared removal is **green**, and the negative control is green.
- before, at BASE `71fa166e96`: `Tests 3 passed`
- after, at HEAD `a99d2041d4`: the whole block, `9 passed`, inside a 28/28 run

Those cases run on walkable history, the PR gate's path, which this change does not touch.

New in the shallow block, a commit that is already on main, rebuilt in a truncated clone:
- **same verdict:** under a main that only moved on and under a main that re-anchored past it, both runs are green on the commit's own anchor, and the removal comparison really ran;
- **teeth:** a schema the commit's anchor recorded and the build dropped, unregistered, is **red under either main**, naming that schema. Under the re-anchored main the old resolver missed this removal and named one of main's additions instead.

## The trade, stated

A truncated history cannot prove `baseRev` is upstream, so a branch that points `baseRev` at its own commit is no longer overridden with main's anchor in a shallow job. That forged rev is refused where history is walkable: `NOT an ancestor of origin/main`, the existing authenticity check, which runs on this repository's PR and merge-queue gate. Both halves are pinned in one case: the shallow run uses the tree's rev, and the walkable run refuses it.

## Tests (all at HEAD `a99d2041d4`)

- `build-schemas-check-mode.test.ts` (vitest `repo` project; the file is about 20 minutes long, so it ran in four `-t` slices): **92 of 92 passed** (13 + 28 + 29 + 22).
- `def-key-collisions.test.ts`, `published-projection-choke-point.test.ts` and `schema-tree-freshness.test.ts` (they spawn, read or digest this script): 35/35 passed.
- `@objectstack/spec` local project: 696 files, 21251 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck`: exit 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json --listFiles` includes both changed files.
- **Ablation**, one-shot. BASE's `build-schemas.ts` was put on disk (hash `a266dcd7e296…` matched BASE's blob), the shallow block ran, then the file was restored (hash `48aab23a9e72…` matched HEAD's blob, `git diff HEAD` empty). Result: **7 failed, 2 passed**. The 2 are the unchanged cases (a real deletion stays red; keys come from git, not the file). The two new cases failed on the old resolver exactly as described above, with `1 schema(s) left the published set … ui/ZzzPublishedOnMainAfterTheCommit`. No `dist/` leg: the test copies `scripts/` and runs it with tsx.
- One fixture in the drift-notice block was re-based without changing its subject. Its shallow state now keeps `merge-base` answerable, because a shallow run with no merge base now anchors on exactly the committed anchor and has no drift left to describe.

## Gates (local, derived with `dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `a99d2041d4`)

`--ran` reconciliation: **65 derived, 60 run, 5 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN** (exit 0).
- 60 ran, every one exit 0. This includes the five spec gates (`check:authorable-surface`, `check:empty-state`, `check:liveness`, `check:strictness-ledger`, `check:variant-docs`), `check:nul-bytes`, `check:published-files`, `check:changeset-gate-self-tests`, `check:adr-0087-registration --base origin/main`, and `check:pm-dispatch-gates`. That battery ran detached; its verdict line was `1913 cases pass` (fast tier).
- NOT MEASURED, `check:dts-closure`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content`: exit 3, prerequisite not met (no workspace `dist/` in this worktree).
- NOT MEASURED, `check:type-check-debt`: it re-measures `tsc` for every package under a closure build and exceeded a 420 s bound (exit 124).

CI runs all five NOT MEASURED families.

## Changeset: `skip-changeset`

`packages/spec/scripts/**` is outside `files[]`. `npm pack --dry-run` lists 0 `scripts/` entries.

Measured: none of this diff's symbols or strings appears in any `files[]` path, nor in `dist/` (each 0 files). Positive controls do hit: `x-unprojectable-branches`, which this script writes into `json-schema/`, is in 6 files; `PageRecordBinding` is in 22 `dist/` files.

The one shipped byte sequence that moves is `json-schema/.build-input-hash-schema`, a freshness digest whose inputs include `scripts/**`, as they do for any test-only spec change. The precedent is `0d43004100`, which changed only this script and carried no changeset.

## Acceptance notes

- **Applies to commits that carry it.** A rebuild runs the script of the commit being built. The 18.0.0-next.3 commit keeps its own resolver forever, so objectui's remote-drop workaround stays needed until its pin moves to a commit carrying this change. Retiring the workaround is objectui's.
- **Boundary, unchanged:** a full clone whose origin/main is OLDER than the commit's own `baseRev` still refuses with `NOT an ancestor of origin/main`. Stale origin/main and a forged anchor are indistinguishable without history, and that refusal is the guard. Noted, not filed; the carrier is none.
- **Inferred, not measured:** why the anchor fetch failed in 13 of objectui's 25 jobs. The annotations show the fetch failed in the re-anchor call and succeeded moments later in the authenticity check. The job logs are on a blob host this container cannot reach (403).
- The origin/main the tree was compared against moved 2 commits after BASE, neither touching `packages/spec/`; the branch was not merged with main.
